title: Continuous Feedback Processing
description: This dataset contains electroencephalography (EEG) recordings from 21 participants performing a continuous feedback prediction task. Participants learned to predict the final level of an animated rising bar under varying conditions of outcome predictability (highly predictable, somewhat predictable, and unpredictable), with performance feedback provided through point rewards. The dataset includes behavioral responses, stimulus timing information, and trigger codes for experimental events, enabling investigation of neural correlates of prediction, feedback processing, and learning under uncertainty.
methods_description: EEG data were collected while participants performed a prediction task involving mouse-based responses to visual cues (gnomes) that varied in outcome predictability. Each trial consisted of a fixation cross (400-600 ms), gnome cue (1500 ms), bar outline (until response), bar animation (1 degree per second), and final outcome display (1000 ms). Trigger codes were recorded to mark fixation onset, cue presentation, bar appearance, participant response, animation start, and animation end.
